purpose: Observe comprehension and musical control separately from scripted action tests
participants: People who have not previously used pre-midi; record prior music/synthesis experience rather than assuming every participant is a beginner
session: One desktop or phone session, approximately 10 minutes; allow normal label hints and exploration
moderator: State the musical goal without naming the correct control. Ask the participant to think aloud. Record assistance; do not convert a coached completion into an unassisted success.

tasks.goal: Choose an instrument and hear it
tasks.observe: Can they distinguish preview, selection and hearing the current edited sound?
Can they predict and hear the cutoff edit with normal help?

tasks.goal: Make the note start slowly, then quickly
tasks.observe: Can they find attack without opening routing controls?

tasks.goal: Make it fade sooner, then later
tasks.observe: Can they distinguish release from volume?
Can they adjust instrument volume and hear the result?

tasks.goal: Save this variation, reload and find it again
tasks.observe: Does the reopened variation match their intended sound and loudness?

tasks.goal: Explore a sound that changes over time
tasks.observe: Can they discover movement routes, adjust amount/speed and describe the audible change?

listeningCriteria: timbre movement is useful and not unintentionally harsh
velocity changes tone as well as loudness
saved variation retains the intended identity
decision: Report task-level findings and revise concrete friction points. Do not infer professional sound quality from waveform differences or newcomer comprehension from successful scripted clicks.
limitation: No human sessions or listening-panel findings have been collected by this worker
